sources_considered.why: Primary supply-and-demand analysis distinguishes conditional exhaustion projections from possible alternatives.
Primary disclosure documents the small-model approach under discussion, including synthetic and selected web data.
Controlled experiments qualify the suggestion that recursive synthetic-data use necessarily deteriorates.
Read the earlier forecast, but used the revised analysis rather than treating the older projected exhaustion date as an observed event.
Describes further research into whether scarcity becomes binding; it does not supply a resolving outcome.

evidence_items.publisher: Villalobos and colleagues / Epoch AI / arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Section 3.1, AI-generated data; abstract for supply projection
evidence_items.explanation: The analysis projects demand reaching the public human-text stock between 2026 and 2032 if trends continue, while discussing synthetic data and other alternatives. This supports concern about a constraint but establishes neither an observed exhaustion event nor that synthetic methods cannot address it.

evidence_items.locator: Key Insights Behind Phi-2; Training Details
evidence_items.explanation: Microsoft describes training Phi-2 using synthetic material and selected web data, while distinguishing these small models from frontier systems. This documents the approach Zitron discusses, but neither its industry-wide prevalence nor a solution to aggregate data scarcity.

The experiments distinguish replacing prior data from accumulating synthetic data alongside it, finding that accumulation avoids collapse in the tested settings. This qualifies the proposed failure mechanism without proving that limited synthetic datasets resolve frontier-wide scarcity.

unresolved_gaps: No observed industry-wide binding shortage is established by the cited projection.
No experiment establishes that the limited synthetic-data methods either remove or necessarily fail to remove the aggregate constraint.
The prevalence and motivation of synthetic-data use are not measured well enough to settle in many cases.
Results about avoiding collapse do not establish unlimited new knowledge or sustained frontier progress.
